**The first public release of AgentBox.**

AgentBox runs a team of AI coding agents on one project, each in a Linux machine of its own, and
lets you direct them from a chat. `agentbox create` gives an agent its own Incus container, a git
worktree on its own branch, Docker, a browser and desktop you can watch and take over, an Android
emulator, and a place for the screenshots, recordings and test reports that prove its work. Several
agents work on the same project at once without colliding on ports, databases or files.

Each project also has a **lead**, its chat: you tell it what you want, and it creates agents, briefs
them with what the project already knows, answers their questions or passes them to you, and tells
you when they're done. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are all driven through it. A desktop app and
a command-line tool talk to one daemon on your machine, which holds all the state; project memory
persists what's been learned across agents and across restarts.

AgentBox runs on Linux on x86_64, and on a Mac, where it runs in a Linux VM it makes with Lima —
though this release only carries the Mac command-line tool, not the desktop app; see **Known
limitations** below. Windows support runs through WSL2. See the README for a full tour, install
steps and a quick start.

**The source is available, under the [Functional Source License](LICENSE) (FSL-1.1-ALv2), not an
open source license.** You can read it, run it, modify it and self-host it; competing with AgentBox
itself is what it restricts. Each version's grant becomes Apache-2.0 two years after that version's
release.

## Downloads

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `AgentBox-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage` | The desktop app, with the `agentbox` command-line tool inside — runs on any Linux distribution |
| `AgentBox-0.1.0-amd64.deb` | The desktop app, for Debian and Ubuntu (`sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.1.0-amd64.deb`) |
| `AgentBox-0.1.0-x64.pacman` | The desktop app, for Arch and its derivatives (`sudo pacman -U AgentBox-0.1.0-x64.pacman`) |
| `AgentBox-0.1.0-x64-setup.exe` | The desktop app for Windows, an installer |
| `AgentBox-0.1.0-x64-portable.exe` | The desktop app for Windows, no installer |
| `agentbox-0.1.0-linux-amd64` / `agentbox-0.1.0-linux-arm64` | The command-line tool and daemon alone, for servers and scripts |
| `agentbox-0.1.0-darwin-arm64` / `agentbox-0.1.0-darwin-amd64` | The command-line tool for a Mac, without the app (the README's "On a Mac") |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` |

There's no Mac desktop app in this release — see **Known limitations**. The Mac command-line tool
above runs `agentbox vm` to make and manage the Lima VM everything else runs in.

## Install

```bash
chmod +x AgentBox-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage
./AgentBox-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or, on Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.1.0-amd64.deb`; on Arch, `sudo pacman -U
AgentBox-0.1.0-x64.pacman`. Both install a launcher alongside the app. On Windows, run the installer
or the portable `.exe`.

On a new machine, open **Settings** in the app and follow its steps, as described in the README's
[Set up](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#set-up). Without the app:
`install -m 0755 agentbox-0.1.0-linux-amd64 ~/.local/bin/agentbox`, then the terminal steps in the
same section. On a Mac, there's only the command-line tool for now: `install -m 0755
agentbox-0.1.0-darwin-arm64 ~/.local/bin/agentbox` (or the `-amd64` build on Intel), then the
README's "On a Mac".

## Known limitations

- **There is no Mac desktop app yet.** Only the command-line tool is released for a Mac so far; the
  app ships once there's an Apple signing certificate to build it with, so it doesn't land unsigned.
  It'll follow in a later release.
- **The Mac port hasn't been tried on real Apple hardware.** The command-line tool and its Lima VM
  are built and have been run in a VM, but not verified on an actual Mac.
- **There is no SECURITY.md yet.** Report a vulnerability to the maintainer privately, not in a
  public issue.
- **This is the first release in this repository.** There are no earlier releases here to compare
  against or upgrade from.
